posts.title: GM reaches $220M settlement over selling drivers' private data | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kirsten Korosec
posts.summary: General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to 36 states to settle allegations that it illegally sold drivers’ private location and behavior data to data brokers, a practice that was exposed by a New York Times investigation. The settlement requires GM to obtain express consent before collecting or sharing driving data and to have a third‑party audit its privacy program, aligning with prior agreements with California and the FTC. Although GM discontinued its Smart Driver program in 2024, the company remains under scrutiny for how it handles connected‑vehicle data and has pledged to stop selling personally identifiable information while still allowing anonymized data sharing with partners. The deal underscores the growing regulatory focus on privacy as automakers increasingly rely on sensor‑rich, software‑centric vehicles and new AI‑powered services like OnStar’s personal assistant.
key_points: GM will pay $220 million to settle claims that it sold private driving data to data brokers.
The settlement mandates express consent for data collection and a third‑party audit of GM’s privacy program.
GM discontinued its Smart Driver program but remains bound by FTC and state orders that restrict data sharing.
GM is positioning its new AI assistant and future connected‑vehicle features around enhanced privacy controls and transparency.

posts.title: The R2 SUV is already Rivian's best-selling vehicle | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sean O'Kane
posts.summary: Rivian’s new R2 SUV has become the company’s best‑selling vehicle in Q3, prompting the automaker to lift its annual delivery guidance to a floor of 67,000 units. The company built 19,751 vehicles and delivered 19,248 in the quarter, a 45% year‑over‑year jump that helped it generate $2.2 billion in revenue while posting a $913 million net loss. The R2, priced just under $60,000, is driving demand in a market that has lost the $7,500 federal EV tax credit, and Rivian plans to introduce lower‑priced trims later this year. This surge in sales marks a turning point for Rivian, which has struggled to ship more than 50,000 vehicles annually for three years.
key_points: R2 SUV became Rivian’s best‑selling vehicle in Q3
Rivian raised its annual delivery guidance to 67,000 units
Q3 production and deliveries rose 45% year‑over‑year
R2 is priced under $60,000 and will see lower‑priced trims later this year

posts.title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings acquires ADT | TechCrunch
posts.author: Julie Bort
posts.summary: Thrive Holdings, a spin‑out of Thrive Capital and backed by OpenAI, has agreed to acquire ADT for $10 per share, valuing the deal at about $7.6 billion in equity and $15.3 billion enterprise value. The acquisition positions Thrive to build a smart‑home security platform, leveraging its AI expertise and OpenAI’s models to develop new physical‑security products. ADT already works with Apple and Google, and the partnership is expected to accelerate the rollout of AI‑powered cameras and other home‑security devices. The deal underscores the growing convergence of AI and physical security as major tech players expand into the smart‑home market.
key_points: Thrive Holdings acquires ADT for $10 per share ($7.6B equity, $15.3B enterprise value).
OpenAI will supply AI models and engineers to help build new security products for Thrive’s portfolio.
The move signals a broader trend of AI integration in physical security and smart‑home ecosystems.

posts.title: Meta quietly launches an AI fashion app called Style Sketch | TechCrunch
posts.author: Aisha Malik
posts.summary: Meta quietly launched Style Sketch, an AI fashion app that builds a virtual closet from Instagram photos or manually uploaded images and suggests outfit combinations tailored to a user’s style. The app offers realistic virtual try‑ons matched to body shape and skin tone, and can generate day‑by‑day outfit plans for trips based on weather and itinerary. It is currently available on iOS and Android in Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. The release is part of Meta’s broader strategy to ship more AI‑driven apps, following recent launches like Waddle World, Pocket, and Vibes.
key_points: Meta launched Style Sketch, an AI fashion app that creates a virtual closet from Instagram photos or manual uploads.
The app suggests outfits, offers realistic try‑ons, and can plan trip outfits using weather and itinerary data.
It is available on iOS and Android in Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand.
Style Sketch is part of Meta’s push to release a larger number of AI‑powered apps.

posts.title: Granola crunches up a dictation feature to compete with Wispr | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: Granola, the meeting‑notetaking startup, has launched an unlimited‑word dictation feature that works across all Mac applications by pressing the Fn key, and it will soon be available on iOS and Windows. The new tool cleans and formats spoken language into text, allowing users to dictate notes, prompts, emails, and messages without limits on any plan. This move positions Granola to compete directly with Wispr, which recently added a meeting‑notetaker to its dictation suite, as both companies are valued at roughly $1.5 billion and $2 billion respectively. The launch reflects a broader trend of voice‑AI startups converging from single‑purpose apps into multi‑feature platforms that capture and process speech for productivity.
key_points: Granola adds unlimited‑word dictation to its meeting‑notetaking suite on Mac.
Feature is available to all plans with no usage limits.
Granola and Wispr are valued at $1.5 billion and $2 billion, respectively.
Voice‑AI apps are moving beyond single‑purpose tools toward comprehensive speech‑capture solutions.

posts.title: Wabi, the AI agent that builds mini apps, now valued at $1.25B after latest round | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Wabi, the AI personal agent founded by former Replika CEO Eugenia Kuyda, closed a $55 million funding round that values the company at $1.25 billion after pivoting from a prompt‑based app builder to a messenger‑style AI that can create mini‑apps for everyday tasks. The round was led by IVP with participation from Andreessen Horowitz, Forerunner, Amazon Alexa Fund, and high‑profile angels including Tobi Lütke, Marc Benioff, Marissa Mayer, Dick Costolo, and Alex Pall. Investors see Wabi’s agentic approach as a timely bet in a market that has seen other AI agents, such as Instinct, raise $1 billion at a $10 billion valuation. The move underscores the growing interest in AI tools that move beyond text boxes to act as personal assistants capable of building functional interfaces on demand.
key_points: Wabi raised $55 million, valuing it at $1.25 billion after pivoting to an AI messenger that builds mini‑apps
The round was led by IVP and included Andreessen Horowitz, Amazon Alexa Fund, and notable angels like Tobi Lütke and Marc Benioff
Investors view Wabi’s agentic model as a strong bet amid a surge of AI‑assistant startups such as Instinct
Founder Eugenia Kuyda brings experience from Replika, positioning Wabi to expand beyond simple prompt‑based apps

posts.title: Amazon reported booming cloud revenue but otherwise missed expectations | TechCrunch
posts.author: Julie Bort
posts.summary: Amazon reported its third‑quarter earnings on Thursday, missing analysts’ expectations for total revenue and earnings per share. The cloud unit, Amazon Web Services, was the bright spot, posting a 39% year‑over‑year revenue growth and beating revenue forecasts. However, free cash flow for the trailing 12 months fell to a negative $42.4 billion, a sharp reversal from the $14.8 billion positive free cash flow reported for the same period ended September 30 2025, largely due to heavy spending on AI. Amazon reiterated a 2026 capital‑expenditure outlook of about $220 billion, roughly matching the $240‑$247 billion net‑sales forecast for the fourth quarter, underscoring the company’s aggressive investment in artificial intelligence.
key_points: Amazon missed Q3 revenue and EPS expectations.
AWS grew 39% YoY and beat revenue forecasts.
Free cash flow turned negative $42.4B, driven by AI spending.
Amazon plans $220B capex for 2026, close to Q4 sales forecast.

posts.title: As search traffic dries up, Reddit announces it's shifting to a logged-in experience | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Reddit announced it will shift to a primarily logged‑in experience as search traffic dries up amid the rise of AI‑powered search. The move is intended to protect data from AI scraping and enable lucrative licensing deals with model providers while helping the company monetize a shrinking user base. Despite a 2% year‑over‑year decline in U.S. daily active users, Reddit’s revenue jumped 53% YoY to $895 million, driven by a 54% rise in advertising and a 35% increase in non‑advertising AI data licensing. The transition will be tested in select markets outside the U.S. in Q4, with no firm global rollout date yet announced.
key_points: Reddit is moving to a logged‑in model to safeguard data and pursue AI licensing amid falling search referrals
Search traffic referrals dropped over 1 million per week in October, contributing to a 2% YoY decline in U.S. daily active users
Revenue grew 53% YoY to $895 million, with advertising up 54% to $847 million and non‑advertising AI data licensing up 35% to $48 million
Logged‑in users offer higher ad value and personalization, and the change will be rolled out gradually starting in Q4

posts.title: Rivian expands joint venture with VW to include AI assistant | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kirsten Korosec
posts.summary: Rivian and Volkswagen Group have expanded their $5.8 billion joint venture to license Rivian’s AI voice‑assistant technology to VW. The assistant, which debuted in Rivian’s R1S SUV and R1T pickup in May 2026 and R2 SUV in October, could first appear in VW’s low‑cost ID EVERY1 hatchback. The move underscores Rivian’s push for vertical integration, allowing it to bundle its electrical architecture, software, and compute platform across partners. VW’s increased investment and the partnership aim to give the German automaker a modern, software‑centric platform that rivals Tesla’s offerings.
key_points: $5.8B joint venture now includes AI assistant licensing
First VW vehicle to use Rivian tech will be ID EVERY1
Rivian’s AI assistant launched in 2026 and supports future third‑party agents
The partnership highlights Rivian’s vertical integration strategy

posts.title: SuperMe raises $20M for its network of AI expert profiles | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: SuperMe, a 2024 startup that builds AI personas from real experts and matches user questions to a curated group chat, has raised $20 million in funding led by Forerunner’s Kirsten Green with participation from Greylock Partners. The platform aggregates knowledge from public sources and connected apps to create AI profiles of industry leaders such as VCs and entrepreneurs, allowing users to ask questions and receive expert‑style answers. While the service remains free for now, SuperMe plans to introduce a paid tier after a limited number of free queries and is hiring to enhance its AI matching algorithms and expand its expert network. The funding underscores the growing interest in hybrid human‑AI knowledge platforms and positions SuperMe to scale its network on both sides of the market.
key_points: SuperMe secured $20M in funding led by Forerunner’s Kirsten Green with Greylock participation
The platform creates AI personas of real experts and matches user queries to a group chat of those personas
The startup plans to monetize after a free tier and is hiring to improve AI matching and expand expert coverage

posts.title: Amazon updates Alexa to help you manage shopping lists and subscriptions and update delivery instructions | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: Amazon has expanded Alexa’s shopping capabilities with over 100 new features that let users create and manage lists, adjust subscription schedules, and edit delivery instructions. The update also lets Alexa answer questions about Prime and Audible memberships, billing, and payment issues. These enhancements come ahead of the holiday season and build on Amazon’s earlier AI‑centric shopping tools such as the shopping assistant and product‑notification service. According to Amazon, agentic features have grown eightfold since the start of the year and more than 400 million consumers have used Alexa for shopping in the past year.
key_points: Alexa now supports over 100 new shopping features, including list management and subscription adjustments.
Users can edit delivery instructions and change addresses directly through voice commands.
The assistant can answer questions about Prime, Audible, billing, and payment issues.
Amazon reports an eight‑fold increase in agentic feature usage and 400 million shoppers using Alexa for purchases.

posts.title: Fan-fiction site Archive of Our Own (AO3) could be offline for up to 4 weeks after security incident | TechCrunch
posts.author: Amanda Silberling
posts.summary: Archive of Our Own (AO3), the fan‑fiction platform run by the nonprofit Organization for Transformative Works, announced that a security incident has forced the site offline and could keep it down for up to four weeks. The incident was discovered during routine maintenance, and while the scope is still being investigated, the team has not ruled out the possibility that user account data—including usernames, emails, IPs, and hashed passwords—may have been accessed. AO3, which is built on Ruby on Rails rather than PHP, is not linked to the recent PHP vulnerabilities, and the organization has urged users to change passwords on other sites as a precaution. The outage has already sparked widespread concern, with the status page receiving millions of views and the community scrambling for updates.
key_points: AO3 offline due to a security incident, with downtime expected up to four weeks
User account data may have been accessed; password changes are advised
The site runs on Ruby on Rails, unrelated to recent PHP vulnerabilities

posts.title: Deepgram acquires Pipecat-maker Daily to bolster its voice AI infrastructure | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: Deepgram has announced the acquisition of Daily, the creators of the open‑source Pipecat framework, without disclosing a price but pledging to keep Pipecat open source. Pipecat orchestrates voice and video streams, integrating speech‑to‑text, large language models, and text‑to‑speech while reducing latency, giving Deepgram a deeper real‑time communication stack. The deal positions Deepgram to expand beyond voice into broader real‑time AI‑native software and to launch the Real‑Time Context Standard, an open protocol for voice agents. Both companies, alumni of Y Combinator’s 2016 batch, emphasize an engineering culture that supports open‑source collaboration and vendor‑neutral ecosystems.
key_points: Deepgram acquires Daily and commits to keeping Pipecat open source
Pipecat is a real‑time orchestration framework for voice, video, STT, LLM, and TTS
The acquisition broadens Deepgram’s real‑time communication capabilities beyond voice
Both firms share a Y Combinator 2016 heritage and a focus on open‑source collaboration

posts.title: Ex-Palantir execs launch Dream with $17M from a16z to build AI world models for construction | TechCrunch
posts.author: Marina Temkin
posts.summary: Ex‑Palantir executives Andy Elder and Arjun Mathur have launched Dream, a startup that uses AI‑powered world models to automate building design and engineering. The company raised $17 million in seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz, with additional backing from SV Angel, XYZ and Zigg Capital. Dream’s “structural cognition” model is trained on over 100 million square feet of U.S. building data and produces structurally sound designs that can replace legacy AEC tools like AutoCAD and Revit. The platform is already deployed on 10 projects in Texas and California and aims to boost productivity in the construction sector, which has seen fewer new buildings and rising costs.
key_points: Dream, founded by former Palantir execs, uses AI world models to generate structurally sound building designs.
The startup secured $17 million in seed funding from Andreessen Horowitz, SV Angel, XYZ and Zigg Capital.
Its “structural cognition” model is trained on more than 100 million square feet of U.S. building data.
Dream is already used on 10 active projects in Texas and California, targeting replacement of legacy AEC software.
